interest: Shows SCAP's 1948-49 deconcentration de-designations, Paramount's property restitution, and bars on trading Japanese securities.
overview: This decimal file (894.5034) encompasses U.S. State Department correspondence, diplomatic despatches, and Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) directives from October 1948 to October 1949 concerning Japanese corporate regulation, Allied property restitution, and securities trading. The documentation centers on three principal subjects: the restitution of prewar corporate property in Japan belonging to Paramount Films, Ltd. through powers of attorney executed for Tokyo attorney Kyozo Yuasa; the progressive deconcentration and zaibatsu-dissolution program under SCAPIN directives 1951, 1958, and 1973, which removed over 120 companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns, accompanied by legal analysis of their ongoing status under Imperial Ordinance No. 567 versus the Anti-Monopoly Law; and inquiries by American investors regarding the purchase and solicitation of Japanese government and corporate bonds, which the Securities and Exchange Commission and State Department confirmed remained prohibited under inter-departmental U.S. policy.

subfiles.about: Transmits an inquiry from Michael Hambury regarding the status of the Nichiman Aluminum Company and advises on channels for contacting former personnel.
subfiles.summary: State tells Athens it has no data on a defunct Nichiman Aluminum firm, suggesting a Tokyo locating agency instead.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 129 to American Mission Athens regarding Nichiman Aluminum Company

subfiles.about: Transmits a power of attorney from Paramount Films President George Weltner in favor of Tokyo attorney Kyozo Yuasa for property restitution in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State sends Paramount's power of attorney to Tokyo attorney Yuasa, to pursue the firm's property restitution in Japan.
subfiles.title: Operations Memorandum to US Reparations and Restitution Delegation Tokyo regarding Paramount Films property restitution
subfiles.to: United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Paramount Films' power of attorney and confirms its transmittal to Tokyo for delivery to attorney Kyozo Yuasa.
subfiles.from: Francis E. Flaherty, Division of Protective Services, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State confirms it sent Paramount's power of attorney to Tokyo for delivery to attorney Yuasa.
subfiles.title: Letter to Corporation Trust Company acknowledging receipt of Paramount Films power of attorney
subfiles.to: Corporation Trust Company, Washington, D. C.

subfiles.about: Reports that Tokyo attorney Kyozo Yuasa inquired about Paramount Films' power of attorney, which had not yet arrived in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Tokyo reports attorney Yuasa never received Paramount's power of attorney, though State says it was mailed in October.
subfiles.title: Operations Memorandum from US Reparations and Restitution Delegation Tokyo regarding missing Paramount Films power of attorney

subfiles.about: Confirms previous transmittal of the Paramount Films power of attorney and offers to secure a duplicate copy if necessary.
subfiles.summary: State confirms Paramount's power of attorney was mailed to Tokyo in October, offering a duplicate if it's lost.
subfiles.title: Operations Memorandum to US Reparations and Restitution Delegation Tokyo confirming dispatch of power of attorney
subfiles.to: United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1951 releasing 73 Japanese companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns and analyzes legal questions under Ordinance No. 567 and the Anti-Monopoly Law.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits SCAPIN 1951 releasing 73 firms from Japan's restricted-concerns list, noting legal debate over continued regulation before transferring oversight to the Fair Trade Commission.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 15 reporting removal of 73 companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to remove seventy-three designated companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: GHQ SCAP issues directive SCAPIN 1951 to the Japanese Government, referencing multiple earlier directives that established the Schedule of Restricted Concerns and added holding company subsidiaries. The memorandum officially removes 73 industrial, chemical, mining, transport, and commercial companies from restricted status. The de-designated firms include former subsidiaries of major zaibatsu combines such as Mitsui, Mitsubishi, Sumitomo, Yasuda, and Matsushita.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1951: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1958 removing an additional fifteen companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1958 releases 15 more Japanese firms from the restricted-concerns schedule.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 40 transmitting SCAPIN 1958 removing 15 companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to remove fifteen designated companies and subsidiaries from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: GHQ SCAP issues directive SCAPIN 1958 to the Japanese Government, referencing prior SCAPINs that added subsidiaries to the restricted list. The memorandum orders the removal of 15 specified corporations—including Shikoku Bank, Kyowa Bank (formerly Japan Savings Bank), Otsu Rubber, and Teikoku Sewing Machine—from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1958: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1973 removing thirty-five companies from the restrictions of the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1973 releases 35 more Japanese firms from the restricted-concerns schedule.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 115 transmitting SCAPIN 1973 releasing 35 companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to remove thirty-five designated companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: GHQ SCAP issues directive SCAPIN 1973 to the Japanese Government, referencing thirteen previous SCAPINs that placed holding company affiliates under restriction. The memorandum releases 35 companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns, including the Imperial Hotel, Dai Nippon Celluloid, Tokyo Building Company, and various shipping, engineering, and manufacturing concerns.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1973: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Refers an inquiry from New York investor E. Allen MacDuffie concerning trading in Japanese and Yugoslav securities to the SEC for response.
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State forwards the SEC an inquiry on whether Americans may trade Japanese and Yugoslav securities.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to SEC referring investor inquiry on Japanese and Yugoslav securities
subfiles.to: Walter C. Louchheim, Jr., Securities and Exchange Commission

subfiles.about: Informs E. Allen MacDuffie that his inquiry regarding the purchase and solicitation of Japanese securities has been referred to the SEC.
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State tells an inquirer his question on soliciting Japanese securities sales falls under SEC jurisdiction.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to E. Allen MacDuffie regarding Japanese securities inquiry

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the State Department referral and encloses a copy of the SEC's reply to E. Allen MacDuffie.
subfiles.from: Walter C. Louchheim, Jr., Securities and Exchange Commission
subfiles.summary: SEC confirms receiving the referred Japanese-securities inquiry, sending State a copy of its reply.
subfiles.title: Letter from SEC to State Department acknowledging referral of Japanese securities inquiry
subfiles.to: Gardner E. Palmer, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Informs E. Allen MacDuffie that U.S. government restrictions against transactions, solicitations, and advertising in Japanese securities remain in effect.
subfiles.from: Walter C. Louchheim, Jr., Securities and Exchange Commission
subfiles.summary: SEC tells an inquirer the ban on trading or advertising Japanese bonds remains in effect, per ongoing inter-agency policy.
subfiles.title: Letter from SEC to E. Allen MacDuffie regarding prohibition on Japanese securities transactions
